newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria depo rates up on higher demand, rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria depo rates up on higher demand, rate rise.

text.p: Bulgaria interbank deposit rates rose on Monday on higher demand for lev funds and a rise in the central bank main interest rate, dealers said.
"Banks were bidding for levs today to boost liquidity after last week's payments of minimum required reserves, corporate tax and Value Added Tax," a dealer said.
Most banks were reluctant to sell foreign currency due to the dollar/mark volatility on global markets on Monday and preferred to raise liquidity through interbank deposits or repurchase agreements.
Depo rates for overnight or two-day deposits were 1.3-1.9 percent annually against 1.2-1.3 percent on Friday.
One-week deposits traded at 1.8-2.75 percent annually against 1.8-2.0 percent and two-week deposits at 2.7-3.0 percent against 2.7 percent.
The average annual interbank deposit rate was 1.55 percent on Friday, lower than 2.62 percent on Thursday, a central bank official said.
The central bank has set its main interest rate at 5.70 percent annually from Monday, higher than 5.59 percent last week. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 91188
